title: tinkerbench-sprint-notes-quentin
content:
Quick context: mid-sprint tinkering day. Mostly short notes, experiments to try, and triage breadcrumbs. Not polished. Use for handoff if I drop off.

Morning triage (03/11)
- Observed p99 spike ~13:20 on canary group A (8k concurrent short prompts). Spike coincides with sudden nvlink errors reported on node-gpu-07: `nvlink reset` messages.
- Symptoms: per-token latency jumps from ~21ms -> 180ms for ~2m window, then back. No model OOMs. Slight tail in queue depth.
- Quick mitigation attempted: moved canary to node-gpu-03 (different rack). Latency stable.
- Follow-ups: collect dmesg + nvidia-smi topo + dcgm logs from node-gpu-07 during window.

Notes and hypotheses
- Hypothesis A: NVLINK path flapping causes GPU DMA fallback -> host staging -> extra memcpy -> big latency tail.
- Hypothesis B: Batch shape skew (sudden flood of 1-token requests mixed with long sequences) caused batching scheduler to emit very large consolidated batches that exceeded preferred kernel tiling and triggered slower kernels. Check batch histograms around spike.
- Hypothesis C: KV cache eviction churn due to sudden spike in unique prefixes; cache invalidation created CPU stalls in the eviction path.

Quick data to gather (commands)
- dmesg | egrep -i "nvlink|nv-host" -T -- since 2026-03-11T13:00
- dcgmi dmon -e to capture detailed GPU errors during next occurrence
- /opt/redwood/bin/runtime-inspect --node node-gpu-07 --range 12:50-13:30 --metrics=batch_hist,kv_evictions,queue_depths > /tmp/triage-07.json
- kubectl logs -n serving runtime-canary-a --since=30m | grep -i "p99\|evict\|fallback"

Short TODOs (prio ordered)
- [P0] Pull dcgm + kernel logs from node-gpu-07 and attach to JIRA-4589 (Quentin). Due: today EOD.
- [P0] Add temporary scheduling rule to avoid node-gpu-07 for canary traffic until we understand (Ravi). Ensure rollout rollback path.
- [P1] Add a histogram of batch sizes to the runtime dashboard (low-res to avoid cost). Wire to per-model dashboard (Maya).
- [P1] Quick micro-experiment: disable prefix KV eviction for model-x-small in canary to see if tail reduces. Note impact on memory growth. (Quentin)
- [P2] Run synthetic test that mixes lengths [1, 64, 1024] with 1:1:1 ratio at 2k qps to reproduce scheduling behavior (loadgen config attached).

Experiment notes (scratch)
- Config tried locally: continuous-batching window=10ms, max-batch=256, kv-eviction-threshold=0.85. Saw p99 drop to baseline but CPU usage rose. Need to measure token-cost delta.
- Alternative: try window=6ms and smaller max-batch=128 -> reduces latency tails, likely at cost of throughput. Worth testing on dedicated node class.
- Quick grep: kernel selection logic picks `fused_attention_v2` for seq_len<=512 else `attention_ref`. If large consolidated batch includes mixed seq lengths, we might be forced into reference kernel. Consider kernel split by per-sample sequence or multi-kernel dispatch.

Kernel / low-level notes
- Check: cudaLaunchKernel failures in stack trace earlier referenced `attention_ref` path. Need to capture backtraces next time.
- Consider adding telemetry to record chosen kernel id + batch composition at time of dispatch (lightweight counters). Add sampling (1/1000 requests).
- nvlink note: some nodes show `inconsistent link width` in dmesg when driver updated last month. Driver rollback/upgrade schedule? File cloud-ticket if repeated.

Handoff / next steps if I'm OOO
- If spike repeats, move canary away from node-gpu-07 (temporary) and escalate to infra with DC: nodes@gitlab-infra. Attach /var/log/nvidia and dcgm snippets.
- If eviction churn suspected: revert kv-eviction tweaks (Quentin) and re-run A/B with and without eviction. Watch memRSS on host and GPU DRAM usage.

Loose thoughts / micro-tasks
- Add a short cron job to pull `batch_size_histogram` every 5m into long-term metrics (store compressed). Helps catch long-tail events.
- Evaluate alternative kernel `mixed-seq-fused` prototype from PR#842 (needs perf test).
- Alias for quick debug: `rdbg node node-gpu-07` -> run the runtime-health-check script.

Unresolved questions
- Was there any maintenance window / network change around 13:15 on 3/11? Ask infra.
- Is there correlation with storage I/O (checkpoint/snapshot) around that time? Check s3/operator logs.

Attachments / references
- local loadgen config: /home/quentin/loadgen/mix_lengths_1-64-1024.yaml (on my laptop)
- PR to watch: GH PR 967 (small batching telemetry)
- Jira: JIRA-4589 (nvlink/latency spike)

Random notes to self
- If I get time: prototype sampled kernel-choice telemetry in a sidecar collector rather than part of hot path. Less invasive.
- Remember to update runbook: add NVLINK flapping section + remediation steps.

End of scratchpad.

(If copied into Confluence, mark as "experimental notes")
